instagram.author: karaloewentheil
instagram.body:
We're taught that self-criticism drives improvement. That if you go easy on yourself, you'll get lazy.

(Before I go any further, I go deeper on this on my YouTube channel. Comment YOUTUBE and I'll send you the link.)

So we talk to ourselves in ways we'd never talk to a child we love, a friend going through something hard, or even a dog we're training.

But self-criticism produces shame and anxiety, and those don't create motivation. They create paralysis. If you criticize yourself every time you sit down to work on a thought pattern, your brain learns to link that work with shame — so it avoids it.

What works is non-judgment. You don't have to love yourself through the process. You just have to stop attacking yourself.

Instead of "I can't believe I thought that, what's wrong with me," try "oh, I just noticed that thought. I wonder where it came from."

That's the difference between a thought you avoid and one that actually changes.

tiktok.author: allychaosmode
tiktok.body:
who can relate!! ⌚️ I’m exhausted from the notifications 😫 I broke up with health and fitness apps (and chose not to get a wearable) during my glp1 journey because I wanted to learn how to trust my own body 🧘🏻‍♀️
Does anyone else feel like health fitness apps, wearables make them less healthy and more anxious, or is that just me? Every fitness app I've ever had, every wellness app, health tracker, wearable tracker has always been pushing me to do more, more, more, more. Close this ring, keep this streak. Do more, do more. Keep working out, keep go, go, go, go, go. And yeah, when I was like, on it, it was really motivating. But if I had so much as one bad week or one bad day, the app would be sending me notifications. For me, these notifications rarely make me feel empowered. They mostly heighten my anxiety. What I have Learned on my six month journey on a G L P1 is that I don't need more nudges and notifications and gamification. I don't need to know that I am 2,000 steps short of my goal. What I want to feel is empowerment. I want to know that I can trust myself to choose the right thing because I want to do it. I didn't go for a walk because I'm short 2,000 steps. I went for a walk because I wanted to move my body, and I knew that walking was what my body needed today. But if I was using most of the wearables or the fitness apps, they would just be like, get on the treadmill, run, run, run more, more, more. And that is why I broke up with all Of the fitness and health apps and the wearables. When I went on my G L P1 journey. And that is why I built my own personal G L P1 app. That doesn't yell at me. In fact, it actually gives me Grace and permission to chill out.
